Our code is 90% caffeine, 10% pure spite, and completely fueled by the delusion that we can fix this bug before the universe collapses. summary:
Missions targeting the lunar south pole—such as NASA's Artemis campaign and Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) landers—face extreme lighting and direct-to-Earth communication constraints. The Moon's slight 1.54 degree axial tilt creates grazing solar angles that cast long shadows across craters, while optical and physical librations continuously modulate Earth line-of-sight. Existing tools like JPL Horizons, QuickMap, and Moon Trek offer deep data but have steep learning curves that slow down rapid scenario evaluation during launch shifts.

HORIZON-X resolves this challenge by translating high-precision astrodynamics ephemerides into an intuitive 3D decision platform. Built with React and Three.js WebGL, it pairs real-time solar and Earth azimuth/elevation vectors against high-resolution lunar topography. The platform features dual interfaces—a Flight Dynamics workspace for mission architects and a jargon-free Science Academy for educators and the public—enabling rapid multi-site comparison and launch window optimization.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

HORIZON-X computes real-time topocentric coordinates for the Sun and Earth from any lunar landing site across past, present, and future dates. The application combines:

  1. Analytical Ephemeris Engine: Computes celestial vectors with sub-milliradian precision, validated against live NASA JPL Horizons API queries (Δθ<0.03∘).
  2. Local Surface 3D Horizon: A Three.js WebGL environment displaying dynamic solar cast shadows, Earth pointing vectors, regolith micro-texture, and an Apollo Lunar Module model.
  3. Solar View (8K Globe): An interactive 3D Moon using high-resolution cartography that visualizes the terminator line, sub-solar point, and orbital planes.
  4. Multi-Site Comparison Matrix: Simultaneous trade-off analysis across Artemis candidate sites, historic Apollo locations, and ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 Shiv Shakti Point.
  5. Dual Operational Modes: Instant toggle between engineering HUD telemetry and a public Science Academy mode with zero technical jargon.

What benefits does it have?

  • Accelerates Mission Planning: Reduces site and launch window re-evaluations from hours of multi-tool queries to seconds.
  • Democratizes Space Science: Public mode makes complex lunar orbital mechanics accessible to students, educators, and enthusiasts.
  • Resilient Operations: Evaluates power generation potential (W/m2) and direct-to-Earth S-band communication margins simultaneously.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages: TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3
  • Frameworks & UI: React 19, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, Canvas Confetti
  • 3D Graphics & Physics: Three.js, WebGL, GLTFLoader, OrbitControls
  • Astrodynamics & Data: NASA JPL Horizons REST API, NASA LOLA DEM, VSOP87/ELP-2000 planetary theory
  • Tooling: Vite, Git, Python

How is your project creative?

Rather than presenting ephemeris data in static tables or disconnected plots, HORIZON-X embeds celestial positions inside a physically scaled 3D lunar surface environment. The platform dynamically aligns solar lighting angles and Earth line-of-sight tracking directly from the lander's perspective, bridging raw mathematical ephemerides with human visual intuition.
